# 4.11.0 — 2026-09-11

27 pull requests merged since 4.10.3 (acme/platform only; acme/mobile ships separately this cycle).

## Features
- Run tokens carry a delegation ceiling; a call above it is parked, never denied silently (#478)
- `oxagen runs export` writes a signed bundle with the verifier script alongside (#480)
- Context recall reports its budget per provider (#474)
- Kill switches gained a deny generation, visible in every later decision (#469)
- Mission Control shows a run's cost basis next to the number (#472)

## Fixes
- Cache reads were mis-attributed when steering landed mid-conversation (#477)
- `github__create_release` schema accepted an empty tag (#475)
- Approval cards no longer expire early when the clock skews (#470)
- Ledger rollups double-counted a retried model call (#468)

## Breaking
- `policy.decide` no longer returns allow for an untainted call with no matching rule; the default is approve (#481)
- `frame.kind` value `tool_call` is renamed `tool.call` in exports (#479)

Unpaged results.title: Why a month of line items should never enter the context window
Unpaged results.why: A tool result is context. Every token the tool returns is paid for on the call that receives it and again on every later turn of the run, because the window carries it forward. aws_billing__get_cost_and_usage returns 41,200 tokens of daily line items and the model sums them to service totals in its head on 86 of 88 runs. The provider can do that sum for free before the result ever leaves AWS.

before.code: # agents/cost_reporter/query.py — as it stands res = ce.get_cost_and_usage( TimePeriod={"Start": start, "End": end}, Granularity="DAILY", GroupBy=[{"Type": "DIMENSION", "Key": "LINKED_ACCOUNT"}, {"Type": "DIMENSION", "Key": "USAGE_TYPE"}], Metrics=["UnblendedCost"]) return res["ResultsByTime"] # ~41k tokens, unpaged

after.code: # agents/cost_reporter/query.py — totals first, rows on demand res = ce.get_cost_and_usage( TimePeriod={"Start": start, "End": end}, Granularity="MONTHLY", GroupBy=[{"Type": "DIMENSION", "Key": "SERVICE"}], Metrics=["UnblendedCost"]) return totals(res) # ~1.9k tokens # exposed as a second tool: aws_billing__get_line_items(service, page)

steps: Split the tool in two: grouped totals for the report, paged line items for a drill-down. The model reaches for the second only when a turn needs a row.
Cap the result body on the registry entry (max_result_tokens) so an unpaged response is truncated with a pointer instead of entering the window whole.
The Spend page attributes each tool's cost as the turn that called it plus the turn that read it, so the saving shows on this row the next time the report runs.
Unpaged results.done: Draft change opened on acme.finops.cost-reporter: grouped totals by service, line items paged behind a second tool. The registry entry caps results at 4,000 tokens.

Repeated shell commands.title: Why re-running the same command costs a turn every time
Repeated shell commands.why: A model in a shell re-runs git status, ls and cargo tree to reassure itself, and the harness obliges. Each re-run costs the call, the result body re-entering the window, and the turn the model spent deciding to look again. On claude_code__Bash 31% of calls were repeats of a command whose result was already in the window, unchanged.

before.code: # agents/stella-ci/harness.yaml — as it stands tools: claude_code__Bash: result_cache: off # every call executes

after.code: # agents/stella-ci/harness.yaml — serve identical commands from the turn window tools: claude_code__Bash: result_cache: scope: turn_window invalidate_on: [write, network] exempt: [date, curl, ps]

steps: The cache keys on the command's input digest and lives for the turn window, so a repeat after a file write or a network call still executes.
Exempt clock and network reads by name; the 51 repeats that legitimately differed were all of that shape.
A served repeat is recorded as a tool.call frame with a cache_hit mark, so the run stays fully sealed and the saving is measurable on this page.
Repeated shell commands.done: result_cache set to turn_window on claude_code__Bash for the Claude Code and Stella harnesses. Recorded as a definition change; takes effect on the next run.

Refetching a stable list.title: Why a list that changes weekly should be fetched weekly
Refetching a stable list.why: The agent's brief says to resolve a channel by name before posting, so it lists the channels first, every run. The list changed twice this month. 341 fetches put 3,400 tokens of channel metadata into 341 contexts, and every later turn on each run carried it forward.

before.code: # agents/release_manager/post.py — as it stands channels = slack.list_channels() # every run target = next(c for c in channels if c.name == name) slack.post_message(target.id, body)

after.code: # agents/release_manager/post.py — workspace cache, 24-hour TTL channels = ctx.cache.get("slack.channels", ttl="24h", fetch=slack.list_channels) target = next(c for c in channels if c.name == name) slack.post_message(target.id, body)

steps: Cache at the workspace, not the run: every agent that posts to Slack shares one fetch a day.
A miss on the name falls through to a fresh fetch, so a channel created an hour ago still resolves.
The cached read is a tool.call frame served from cache, so the run is still sealed and the saving shows on this row.
Refetching a stable list.done: Workspace cache slack.channels set with a 24-hour TTL. Both agents that post to Slack read it on their next run.

Cache misses after a stable prefix chang.title: Why a mid-day steering publish empties the prompt cache
Cache misses after a stable prefix chang.why: Every model call on a run starts with the same system block: the compiled steering bundle, then the tool definitions. Providers cache that prefix by content hash. Publish a steering record and the bundle hash changes, so every live conversation pays full input price on its next call and again on every call until the new prefix is warm. The runs that were live when Priya merged paid that twice: once for the miss, once because their old prefix was still in the cache and never read again.

before.code: # .oxagen/workspace.toml — as it stands [context] publish = "on_merge" # bundle bumps the moment the PR merges

after.code: # .oxagen/workspace.toml — batch publications to a window [context] publish = "windowed" publish_windows = ["00:00Z", "12:00Z"] drain_live_runs = true # live runs finish on the old bundle

steps: Merged records queue until the next window instead of bumping the bundle at once.
Runs that are live at the window keep their prefix to the end; new runs start on the new bundle.
Urgent records can still publish now, from the record's PR, with the cost shown before you confirm.
Cache misses after a stable prefix chang.done: Publication windows set to 00:00Z and 12:00Z. Merged records now queue for the next window; the change is a Context PR on acme/platform.

Tool-list bloat.title: Why a 52-tool belt costs you on every call
Tool-list bloat.why: Tool definitions are not free context. Every model call carries the JSON schema of every tool on the belt, and the model reads all of it before it reads the task. On acme.core.triage that block is 9,140 tokens, and 34 of the 52 tools were never called in 1,340 runs. The agent was wrapped with each MCP server's full export, which is the default when a wrap grants a server instead of a tool.

before.code: # agents/triage/wrap.yaml — as it stands grants: - server: github # 41 tools · 12 called - server: linear # 18 tools · 4 called - server: slack # 14 tools · 2 called

after.code: # agents/triage/wrap.yaml — grant the 18 tools the runs call grants: - server: github tools: [get_issue, list_commits, add_labels, search__code, get_file_contents, …] - server: linear tools: [get_issue, update_issue, list_labels, create_comment] - server: slack tools: [post_message, get_thread]

steps: Grant tools, not servers. The belt is compiled from the grants, so the definition block shrinks to what is listed.
Set beltMode to searchable if the agent sometimes needs a rare tool: it then sees a one-line index and fetches a definition on demand.
A tool that a run calls without a grant is denied and recorded, so a narrowing that was too tight shows up as a policy.decision frame, not a silent failure.
Tool-list bloat.done: Draft wrap opened with the 18 called tools granted. Review it and publish; the belt recompiles on the next run.

Wrong tier.title: Why retries on this agent escalate to the flagship tier
Wrong tier.why: The harness routes each step by tier: light for classification-shaped work, complex for reasoning. When a light-tier call fails or times out, the retry takes the fallback route, and this agent's fallback is the workspace default, which is the complex tier. So every transient timeout on a 300-token label call is retried on claude-opus-5 at 15× the price, and 188 of 191 such retries produced the same label the light tier had already given on the same input.

before.code: # agents/triage/agent.yaml — as it stands model: route: light # fallback: inherited — workspace default is "complex"

after.code: # agents/triage/agent.yaml — pin the fallback model: route: light fallback: light # retry on the same tier retry: max: 2 backoff_ms: 400

steps: Pin fallback to the same tier for classification agents. Escalation is for reasoning steps that ran out of capability, not for timeouts.
Keep escalation for the 3 in 191 that differed: set escalate_on to disagreement so a second light call that disagrees with the first goes to the complex tier.
The route each call took is on its frame as model, so the Spend page shows the fix taking effect the same day.
Wrong tier.done: Fallback pinned to the light tier for acme.core.triage. Recorded as a definition change; takes effect on the next run.

Unproductive tail.title: Why this agent keeps stepping after the work is done
Unproductive tail.why: A custom agent loop that runs until the model says it is finished will, on most models, re-read what it just wrote, list the directory again, and ask itself whether it is done, several times over. None of that produces a side effect the run keeps. On acme.core.docs-writer those tail steps average 2.1 model calls each, and on 41 of 64 runs there were six or more of them after the last kept write.

before.code: # agents/docs_writer/loop.py — as it stands while not done: step = agent.next_step(ctx) ctx.apply(step) done = step.kind == "final" # the model decides when to stop

after.code: # agents/docs_writer/loop.py — stop after two unproductive steps idle = 0 while not done: step = agent.next_step(ctx) effect = ctx.apply(step) idle = 0 if effect.kept else idle + 1 done = step.kind == "final" or idle >= 2 # effect.kept comes from the gateway: did the side effect survive to the sealed run?

steps: Count unproductive steps from the gateway's own signal: a step is productive when its side effect is kept in the sealed run.
Two consecutive unproductive steps is the workspace's baseline for the other agents; tune it on the agent, not globally.
The witness already confirms the output is identical before and after the tail, so cutting it changes nothing the run keeps.
Unproductive tail.done: Stop rule after two unproductive steps recorded as a definition change on acme.core.docs-writer. The agent's loop reads it from the bundle.

Cache writes never read.title: Why cache writes on one-turn runs are a pure premium
Cache writes never read.why: A cache write costs 1.25× the input price and pays back only if a later call reads the prefix inside the TTL. Priya's invoice runs are one turn each, scheduled forty minutes apart, and the agent's request builder marks the system block cacheable on every call. So each run writes an 18,400-token prefix that expires unread. The premium was the whole cost of the write.

before.code: # agents/invoice_bot/request.py — as it stands system = [{"type": "text", "text": SYSTEM, "cache_control": {"type": "ephemeral"}}] # on every call

after.code: # agents/invoice_bot/request.py — write the cache only when a read will follow cacheable = run.expected_turns > 1 or schedule.next_within(minutes=5) system = [{"type": "text", "text": SYSTEM, **({"cache_control": {"type": "ephemeral"}} if cacheable else {})}]

steps: Write the cache when a read is likely: multi-turn runs, or a schedule that fires again inside the TTL.
Alternatively batch the invoice runs: 28 runs five minutes apart would share one write and read it 27 times.
The gateway records cache_write and cache_read on every frame, so the Spend page shows the premium disappearing the next day.
Cache writes never read.action: Stop writing cache on one-turn runs
Cache writes never read.done: Recorded on acme.finops.invoice-bot: cache writes only when a read is expected. Priya is notified as the operator.

INCIDENTS.title: Money moved that Oxagen did not govern
INCIDENTS.detail: Stripe charge ch_3Qa8 for $18.00 USD settled against the governed connection con_01K2A9 with no receipt. Every call Oxagen dispatched that day reconciles; this one has no frame, so it did not come through the tool gateway.
INCIDENTS.resolution: Open. Dana Okafor is tracing the charge against the Stripe dashboard audit log. Until it closes, reconciliation for 2026-09 cannot report 100% of governed spend, and the Spend page says so.

INCIDENTS.title: Assurance case not applicable on the shared plane
INCIDENTS.detail: One suite case, “modify a receipt after the fact”, cannot run where object lock is off. It is reported as not applicable, never as passed.
INCIDENTS.resolution: Open. Object lock in compliance mode needs a dedicated data plane, which is an Enterprise plan change. The owner has until 2026-09-30 to decide, or to accept the gap in writing.

INCIDENTS.title: Tainted argument on a shell call, raised to approval; the approval expired
INCIDENTS.detail: An argument to bash__run@1 derived from a tool output the run had ingested. Taint raised the decision from allow to approve; no approver answered within 10 minutes.
INCIDENTS.resolution: Expired, so denied. The denial and its reason reached the model as the permission decision reason; the run continued without the call and closed clean.

INCIDENTS.title: Witness fingerprint moved during a run
INCIDENTS.detail: The witness branch was rebased while the run was live, so the sealed fingerprint no longer matched the one taken at open. The seal records verdict tampered, and a seal is never overwritten.
INCIDENTS.resolution: A developer rebased the witness branch by hand. The task was re-run as run_01K5RQ4B9C7XTN2P, which proved at 09:02 with oracle test_flip.

INCIDENTS.title: Chain verification failed on an export segment
INCIDENTS.detail: The bundle verifier reported a Merkle root mismatch on one archive segment. A tampered receipt and a truncated read look identical to the verifier, so the incident opens at warning until the cause is known.
INCIDENTS.resolution: Object storage returned a short read on a multipart object. Segment re-read, root matched, bundle re-signed and re-issued. No frame body changed; digests identical.

INCIDENTS.title: Harness permission hooks removed mid-run
INCIDENTS.detail: The Claude Code harness on mbp-01 reported its permission hooks gone between two steps. The gateway dropped the run to observe tier for its remainder and labeled every later frame client-attested.
INCIDENTS.resolution: A local harness update rewrote settings.json. Hooks restored and the host re-enrolled through the wrapper. Frames from the observe window stay labeled as such; the label is never upgraded after the fact.

INCIDENTS.title: Run token presented directly to a tool server
INCIDENTS.detail: A run token was sent to api.github.com instead of the tool gateway. GitHub rejected it; the gateway recorded the attempt. Tool servers accept broker credentials only, so the token was never valid there.
INCIDENTS.resolution: A retry path in a custom script bypassed the MCP endpoint. Script corrected; no credential was exposed.
